topic: Interference, grounding and bonding; speech processing, S meters and band edges (G4C, G4D; 23 pool questions)

questions.question: Which of the following might be useful in reducing RF interference to audio frequency circuits?

choices.A: Bypass inductor

questions.question: Which of the following could be a cause of interference covering a wide range of frequencies?

choices.A: Not using a balun or line isolator to feed balanced antennas
choices.B: Lack of rectification of the transmitter’s signal in power conductors
choices.C: Arcing at a poor electrical connection
choices.D: Using a balun to feed an unbalanced antenna

questions.answer: Arcing at a poor electrical connection

questions.question: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a single sideband phone transmitter?

choices.A: A steady hum whenever the transmitter is on the air

questions.question: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a CW transmitter?

choices.A: On-and-off humming or clicking
choices.B: A CW signal at a nearly pure audio frequency

questions.question: What is a possible cause of high voltages that produce RF burns?

choices.A: Flat braid rather than round wire has been used for the ground wire
choices.B: Insulated wire has been used for the ground wire
choices.D: The ground wire has high impedance on that frequency

questions.answer: The ground wire has high impedance on that frequency

questions.question: What is a possible effect of a resonant ground connection?

choices.A: Overheating of ground straps
choices.C: High RF voltages on the enclosures of station equipment

questions.answer: High RF voltages on the enclosures of station equipment

questions.question: Why should soldered joints not be used in lightning protection ground connections?

choices.A: A soldered joint will likely be destroyed by the heat of a lightning strike
choices.B: Solder flux will prevent a low conductivity connection
choices.C: Solder has too high a dielectric constant to provide adequate lightning protection

questions.answer: A soldered joint will likely be destroyed by the heat of a lightning strike

questions.question: Which of the following would reduce RF interference caused by common-mode current on an audio cable?

choices.A: Place a ferrite choke on the cable
choices.B: Connect the center conductor to the shield of all cables to short circuit the RFI signal
choices.C: Ground the center conductor of the audio cable causing the interference
choices.D: Add an additional insulating jacket to the cable

questions.answer: Place a ferrite choke on the cable

questions.question: How can the effects of ground loops be minimized?

choices.A: Connect all ground conductors in series
choices.B: Connect the AC neutral conductor to the ground wire
choices.C: Avoid using lock washers and star washers when making ground connections

questions.question: What could be a symptom caused by a ground loop in your station’s audio connections?

choices.A: You receive reports of “hum” on your station’s transmitted signal
choices.B: The SWR reading for one or more antennas is suddenly very high
choices.C: An item of station equipment starts to draw excessive amounts of current
choices.D: You receive reports of harmonic interference from your station

questions.answer: You receive reports of “hum” on your station’s transmitted signal

questions.question: What technique helps to minimize RF “hot spots” in an amateur station?

choices.A: Building all equipment in a metal enclosure
choices.D: Placing low-pass filters on all feed lines

questions.question: Why must all metal enclosures of station equipment be grounded?

choices.A: It prevents a blown fuse in the event of an internal short circuit
choices.C: It ensures that the neutral wire is grounded
choices.D: It ensures that hazardous voltages cannot appear on the chassis

questions.answer: It ensures that hazardous voltages cannot appear on the chassis

questions.question: What is the purpose of a speech processor in a transceiver?

choices.A: Increase the apparent loudness of transmitted voice signals
choices.B: Increase transmitter bass response for more natural-sounding SSB signals
choices.D: Decrease high-frequency voice output to prevent out-of-band operation

questions.answer: Increase the apparent loudness of transmitted voice signals

questions.question: How does a speech processor affect a single sideband phone signal?

choices.A: It increases peak power

questions.question: What is the effect of an incorrectly adjusted speech processor?

choices.A: Distorted speech

questions.question: What does an S meter measure?

choices.A: Carrier suppression

questions.question: How does a signal that reads 20 dB over S9 compare to one that reads S9 on a receiver, assuming a properly calibrated S meter?

choices.A: It is 10 times less powerful

questions.question: How much change in signal strength is typically represented by one S unit?

choices.A: 6 dB

questions.question: How much must the power output of a transmitter be raised to change the S meter reading on a distant receiver from S8 to S9?

choices.A: Approximately 1.5 times

questions.question: What frequency range is occupied by a 3 kHz LSB signal when the displayed carrier frequency is set to 7.178 MHz?

choices.A: 7.178 MHz to 7.181 MHz

questions.question: What frequency range is occupied by a 3 kHz USB signal with the displayed carrier frequency set to 14.347 MHz?

choices.A: 14.347 MHz to 14.647 MHz

questions.question: How close to the lower edge of a band’s phone segment should your displayed carrier frequency be when using 3 kHz wide LSB?

choices.A: At least 3 kHz above the edge of the segment
choices.B: At least 3 kHz below the edge of the segment
choices.C: At least 1 kHz below the edge of the segment
choices.D: At least 1 kHz above the edge of the segment

questions.answer: At least 3 kHz above the edge of the segment

questions.question: How close to the upper edge of a band’s phone segment should your displayed carrier frequency be when using 3 kHz wide USB?

choices.A: At least 3 kHz above the edge of the band
choices.B: At least 3 kHz below the edge of the band
choices.C: At least 1 kHz above the edge of the segment
choices.D: At least 1 kHz below the edge of the segment

questions.answer: At least 3 kHz below the edge of the band
